title: Docs: Shadow traffic + quality metrics quickstart (enablement, sampling, interpretation)
creator: Monica Patel
project: Shadow traffic tool for eval metrics
description:
Create end-user docs + quickstart for Shadow Traffic experiments and quality metrics. Docs should cover: enabling shadowing on a route/rollout, choosing sampling rates, interpreting quality deltas (including confidence intervals), and common pitfalls/troubleshooting. Must include clear warnings about cost/overhead and data retention/redaction defaults (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Target audience: platform/ML engineers rolling out model/version/quantization changes safely.

Primary surfaces:
- Redwood Docs (public) quickstart
- Console UX callouts (copy/tooltips reuse)
- SDK/API snippets (Python/TS) aligned with Console backend contract

Out of scope: full eval-harness authoring guide (separate doc) and deep statistical methodology reference (link out to observability standard).
acceptance_criteria:
1) A published docs page exists titled "Shadow traffic quality metrics quickstart" with a guided flow from "create experiment" -> "watch scoring" -> "interpret deltas" -> "graduation/rollback".
2) Includes at least one Console-driven workflow and one API-driven workflow.
3) Contains explicit guidance for sampling and minimum sample sizes (rules of thumb) + how to tell if results are underpowered.
4) Documents default metric bundle v1 and what each metric does/does not mean.
5) Documents failure modes and what happens when scoring/telemetry is delayed (fail-open behavior).
6) Contains a troubleshooting section mapping common symptoms to likely causes and mitigations.
7) Security/compliance callouts included: retention windows, redaction, access controls, Private constraints.
8) Reviewed/approved by: Product (Marissa Cole), Applied ML (Jonas Weber or Selene Huang), SRE (Sean Gallagher), Security (Marcus Lin) for accuracy of warnings/guardrails.
9) Links to runbook and relevant Console pages; versioned with release notes (beta -> GA).
implementation_notes:
Doc should match beta behavior:
- Shadowing is "fail-open": control response always returns; shadow path timeouts/errors should not impact user latency.
- Shadow requests are sampled deterministically (consistent bucketing) so comparisons remain stable across time windows.
- Metrics are computed asynchronously; dashboards may lag behind real time (call out expected delay + how to monitor scoring lag).
- Cardinality guardrails: do not encourage users to add high-cardinality tags/headers; document allowed dimensions and safe segmentation patterns.

Where to link:
- Console shadow experiment pages (create/view)
- Runbook: shadow traffic rollout/rollback
- Observability standard: naming + CI conventions
- Data retention + redaction policy

Tone: practical and cautionary (cost + safety), but action-oriented. Include “when not to use shadow traffic” (e.g., extremely sensitive prompts without redaction plan, extremely high-QPS routes without overhead budget).
doc_outline_draft:
Proposed page structure (single quickstart + linked references):

1. What is shadow traffic quality testing?
- Mirrors a sampled subset of production requests to candidate variants.
- Scores candidate outputs asynchronously (rubrics + heuristics).
- Surfaces quality deltas alongside latency/cost/error without changing user responses.

2. Prerequisites
- Permissions: required roles to create experiments / view examples.
- Data handling: confirm retention/redaction defaults for your deployment mode.
- Cost: scoring + shadow inference overhead; start low.

3. Quickstart (Console)
A) Create a Shadow Experiment
- Select a route (or attach to an active rollout/canary)
- Choose control vs shadow variant(s): model version, quantization profile, prompt template, routing policy
- Set sampling rate and max shadow RPS (if available)
- Choose metric bundle v1
- Save + start

B) Verify it’s healthy
- Check: shadow target error rate, scoring queue lag, ingestion lag
- Confirm control path unaffected (p99 latency unchanged)

C) Read the results
- Where to find: Quality Deltas tab
- How to read: delta charts + confidence bands + segments
- What to do: continue, increase sampling, stop, or rollback candidate

4. Quickstart (API)
- Create experiment via API
- Poll aggregates
- Fetch examples (with redaction notes)

5. Choosing sampling rates (rules of thumb)
- Start at 0.5–1% for high-QPS routes; 5% for low-QPS internal routes.
- Prefer deterministic sampling; keep rate constant during an experiment.
- Stop criteria: stable CI bounds; avoid peeking too early.

6. Metrics shipped in v1 (and caveats)
- Refusal rate (what counts as refusal; false positives)
- Format adherence (structured output / JSON validity)
- Instruction-following rubric score (model-graded; calibration notes)
- Safety rubric (high-level; not a replacement for full safety eval)

7. Common pitfalls
- Underpowered experiments (wide confidence intervals)
- Mixing rubric versions across runs
- Sampling changes mid-stream
- High-cardinality segmentation causing missing charts/limited breakdowns
- Streaming responses (partial capture semantics)

8. Troubleshooting
- "No quality data" -> scoring lag / ingestion lag
- "Shadow errors spike" -> shadow target capacity / timeouts
- "Latency increased" -> misconfigured shadow timeouts or backpressure not tripping
- "Cardinality alerts" -> too many labels/headers; reduce segmentation

9. Next steps
- Attach experiment to rollout guardrails (advisory thresholds)
- Export results / share with stakeholders
- Run a prompt-set eval in eval-harness for deeper coverage

Appendix: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private differences
- Retention defaults and configuration knobs
- Region/data residency constraints
- Air-gapped scoring options (Private) / external evaluator guidance
api_snippet_notes:
Ensure examples match actual naming in Console backend + SDKs.
- Prefer showing SDK usage first (Python), then raw REST.
- Avoid exposing internal IDs; show how to use route name + variant refs.
- Include explicit timeout and fail-open notes (non-configurable vs configurable fields).

Placeholder field names to align with ENG-5407 contract:
- route_id or route_name
- control_variant_id
- shadow_variant_ids[]
- sampling_rate
- rubric_version
- retention_mode (if exposed)
- max_shadow_qps (if supported)

Docs should not imply that customers can upload arbitrary custom code in v1.
